Behavior
"Separate" shows Context and Filtered as two tabs you switch between. "Stacked" shows both at once, split top/bottom, as a single "Stacked" tab alongside Table/Plot.
Whether the row-action buttons next to the level filter (Filter after this, Add to selection, …) show their name. "On hover" (default) reveals it only while pointing at one, expanding it into a pill. "Never" keeps them plain icons (still explained by their tooltip); "Always" keeps every label expanded permanently.
Same idea, for the buttons in each view's own toolbar (Context/Filtered/Table/Plot) — these expand into a rounded rectangle rather than a pill. Set independently from the Filter-Toolbar above.
A filter you've never viewed before always opens to Filtered. For one you've already viewed, "Remember last view" (default) reopens whichever tab — Context, Filtered, Table, or Plot — you left it on. "Always Filtered" reopens it to Filtered every time instead.
"Start" stays at the top (default). "End" scrolls to and stays at the bottom — with Tailing on, following begins immediately from there.
Only effective in the desktop build.
Only effective in the desktop build. The window's close button hides it to the tray instead of quitting; right-click the tray icon to quit for real.
Used when copying extraction table cells (Ctrl+C) or exporting as CSV. "Auto" guesses from the browser's language, which doesn't always match what your spreadsheet app expects — pick one explicitly if pasted numbers come out wrong.
Hover-to-expand panels
Hovering the collapsed sidebar temporarily expands it. Turn off to expand it only by clicking.
Hovering the collapsed entry detail panel temporarily expands it. Turn off to expand it only by clicking.
Context view
The Context view shows the active filter's matches with everything it rejected hidden between them. "Auto expand around the selected row" (the default) keeps the rest hidden but reveals a few lines above and below whatever row you land on — double-clicking or pressing Enter on a row in the Filtered view, walking match to match with the ‹ / › arrows, or simply clicking another match — and hides the ones the previous jump revealed again, so the context follows you instead of piling up. Lines you reveal or collapse by hand are left alone by that and keep the state you gave them. "Collapsed" reveals nothing until you ask for it; "Expanded" starts with the whole file shown, still collapsible run by run. A jump to a row that isn't a match always reveals it, whichever option is picked — otherwise it would have nowhere to be shown. The Stacked layout always starts fully expanded regardless of this setting (its Context pane sits right next to the plain Filtered result, so there's less need to hide anything there) — this only governs the Context tab in Tabs layout.
How many hidden lines one expansion step reveals in each direction — so the default 10 gives you 10 lines above and 10 below the row you land on. The same number is what a "Show more (+n)" row adds to a run that is already open; the "… N lines" row above/below it always reveals everything that is left in one go. The two directions of a hidden stretch are operated separately: revealing more above never also reveals more below.
Timeline minimap
Turn this on to hide the minimap's outer "covered timespan" box while the Context view is the one showing — the inner "currently rendered" box stays visible and tracks that view's own scroll position instead. Both boxes keep their normal behavior in the Filtered and Stacked views. (Off by default. This dates from when that view always showed the whole file, which made the outer box meaningless there; now that it shows the active filter's own result, the box is informative again — kept as an opt-out for anyone who prefers the quieter minimap.)
Filter tree
"Automatic" — clicking a level button writes a real, visible/undoable filter node into the tree at the current position. "Manual" — the level bar keeps its original quick, tree-independent toggle, with a separate "Add to tree" button to push the current selection in on demand.
Switching the active filter (tree click or Alt+Arrow) while the current row doesn't match it shows that row at its would-be position as a temporary anchor, not a real bookmark. "Off" never draws it (Up/Down still remembers its position). "Persistent" keeps it shown until a different row is selected. "Fade" shows it briefly, then removes it after the configured duration.
When the active filter switches to one belonging to a different file than the currently selected row, still show that row as a temporary anchor. Turn off to only show the anchor when switching filters within the same file.
Anchor fade duration
How long the temporary anchor stays visible before it's removed.
3s
Text-match highlighting
Your standing preference for text-filter match highlighting — always editable here regardless of the view bar's on/off button, which just quickly toggles whatever is configured below.
Marks matches inline in the log rows themselves, in both the Filtered and the Context view — in Stacked layout the same entry is on screen in both panes at once, so marking it in only one of them read as two different rows.
Marks matches in the bottom entry-detail panel. Independent of the row toggle above — turn both on for both.
The icon and the TXT/LNK/... abbreviation both say the same thing about a filter's type — pick which one shows, at the icon's own position, instead of both.
Log Formats
Define additional log formats and map filenames to them by pattern — the default format works with zero configuration.
Add log format
%d/%date %p/%level %t/%thread %c/%logger %M/%method %m/%message %n — \t \n \\ stand for a literal tab/newline/backslash.
Needs a (?<message>...) named group; (?<ts>...)/(?<level>...)/(?<thread>...)/(?<location>...)/(?<method>...) are optional.
Tokens: yyyy MM dd HH mm ss SSS. Empty = free-form (best effort).
Only checked levels get a quick-filter button for files using this format; anything else falls into OTHER. Custom names match a line's level text exactly (case-insensitive) and get a color from a rotating palette.
Filename rules — first matching pattern wins; files matching none use the default format
